subject: AcmeBank evaluation: model recommendations, datasets, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmebank.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@acmebank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from today’s discovery (Redwood evals)

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the context on AcmeBank’s customer support use case and the latency/cost constraints you flagged. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

- Goal: run customer-specific evals against your support response reranking + summarization workload to validate model fit and quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Scope: 1k–5k labeled examples for an initial benchmark (we discussed starting with ~2k).
- Success criteria: accuracy/ROUGE for summarization, MRR/NDCG for reranking; baseline is your current in-house model (you said ~85% satisfaction on sampled tickets).

Recommended next actions:
1) You share a sample dataset (2k rows, see sample format attached: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv).
2) We run three model families in parallel on Redwood (detailed config below) and provide per-model token-cost estimates, latency percentiles, and quality metrics.
3) We run a regression check vs your baseline and provide example failcases + prompt-set recommendations.

Preliminary model recommendations (so you can think about alignment):
- Redwood/gpt-3.5-highperf (dense fp16) — strong quality/latency tradeoff for summarization
- Redwood/opt-8q (8-bit quant) — lower cost, slightly higher variance on longer contexts
- open-llama-3-7b (quant) — lowest cost baseline for edge cases; useful for routing fallback

I attached a short runbook (redwood_eval_runbook.pdf) with dataset format and scoring examples. If this plan looks good, can you confirm we should proceed with a 2k sample? Once confirmed, Dev will provision the eval environment and share an S3 bucket + upload instructions.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv (CSV with headers: id,input,expected_output,metadata), redwood_eval_runbook.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@acmebank.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmebank.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today’s discovery (Redwood evals)

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we send data:

1) For the 2k sample, is it OK if some rows don’t have a perfect "expected_output" (we have fuzzy labels)?
2) What exact metrics will you run by default? We care most about relevance/precision for rerank, and ROUGE-1/2 for summarization.
3) Any data handling / encryption requirements we need to include for procurement? (SOC 2 evidence was mentioned).

We can provide a sanitized export by EOW if that timeline works. Also looping Jorge (ops) for the technical upload.

— Samantha
Director, Customer Experience | AcmeBank
samantha.lee@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmebank.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@acmebank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today’s discovery (Redwood evals)

Great questions — answers below and a little more detail so procurement/ops have what they need:

1) Labels: fuzzy labels are fine. We support graded scoring (confidence buckets) and pairwise judgements. If expected_output is missing, we fall back to reference-free metrics and human-in-the-loop checks. See runbook section "labeling guidance."

2) Default metrics we’ll produce:
   - Summarization: ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and a small crowdsourced human pass for edgecases
   - Reranking: MRR, NDCG@5, Precision@1/3, and an error-rate on negative sampling
   - Cost/Lat: p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, and unit token cost estimates using your projected throughput

3) Data handling / procurement notes:
   - We can accept encrypted S3 uploads (AES-256). Dev will share a pre-signed URL + envelope encryption guidance.
   - Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; procurement can request SOC evidence via this DocuSign link (https://hub.redwood.ai/soct2-request).

Dataset format (short):
- CSV or JSONL accepted. CSV columns: id, input, expected_output, metadata
- metadata should be a JSON string with fields: customer_segment, channel, created_at (ISO8601), sample_weight
- For reranking tasks, include fields: candidate_pool (JSON array of candidates), label (rank index or relevance score)

Scoring criteria and regression checks:
- We’ll compute relative delta vs your baseline for each metric. Regression alert threshold default: 2.5% absolute drop in primary metric (configurable).
- We’ll surface example prompts that cause >X divergence and suggest prompt/template fixes or model variant fallbacks.

Model recommendations (finalized for the run):
- Run A (quality): redwood/gpt-3.5-highperf, context 2k, greedy+temperature=0.0 for deterministic eval
- Run B (cost-aware): redwood/opt-8q, 8-bit quant, context 2k, greedy
- Run C (baseline fast): open-llama-3-7b-quant, lower token cost, measure tail latencies

Attachments: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv (example), redwood_eval_runbook.pdf (detailed steps). I included a sample scoring script snippet in the runbook.

If that looks good, confirm the 2k sample timeline and we’ll start provisioning.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today’s discovery (Redwood evals)

Hi Samantha — looping in technical steps so Jorge / procurement can move forward:

1) I’ll provision a temporary eval project in your preferred region (us-west1) and create an S3 bucket with AES-256 at rest. Expect pre-signed upload links from me within 24 hours after you confirm the sample.
2) Please upload the sample as: s3://redwood-acme-evals/sample/20260720-acme-sample.csv (we’ll share the exact presigned URL).
3) We’ll kick off three parallel runs described by Marissa and deliver a short report within 3 business days after we have the data. The report will include: metric tables, cost estimates, latency percentiles, example failcases, and recommended prompt changes.

Notes on credentials and security: we support customer-managed KMS for envelope keys if needed; procurement should email procurement@redwood.ai with the KMS request form. SOC 2 evidence available on request (Marissa linked the request flow).

Next steps for you: confirm EOW upload and whether you want us to redact PII (we can run an automated redaction pass if you prefer; it will add ~1 business day). Once you confirm, I’ll send the presigned URL and bootstrap the project.

— Dev
